newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin praises Annan, says Russia to pay UN debts.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin praises Annan, says Russia to pay UN debts.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin said on Saturday Russia would settle its debts to the United Nations and increase its cooperation with the organisation.

During a meeting in the Kremlin with Kofi Annan, Yeltsin praised the new Secretary-General's "energetic work" on reorganisation. Annan was to fly to St Petersburg later on Saturday and conclude a four-day visit to Russia on Sunday.
"We will develop our cooperation with the U.N.," Yeltsin said at the start of their meeting. "We will settle up, in a disciplined way as is planned, without creating new debts."
Russia is the second biggest debtor to the U.N., though it owes a fraction of what is owed by the United States, which owes well over half the organisation's $2.3 billion deficit.

Russia paid $305 million to the organisation last year and has promised to pay off what else is due. In September last year it owed some $300 million for peacekeeping operations -- which are the main component of member countries' debts to the U.N.
